units: <cite ref="Onkelos Exodus 12:4">Targ. Ex. XII, 4</cite> (Y. ed. Vien. <he>שיכ׳</he>, corr. acc.).—Pl. <cite ref="U00786"><he>שִׁיבְבִין</he></cite>, <he>שִׁיבְבֵי</he>.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Deuteronomy 24:17">Targ. Y. Deut. XXIV, 17</cite> (not <he>שיבבון</he>).
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on II Kings 4:3">Targ. II Kings IV, 3</cite> (ed. Wil. <he>שְׁבֵבַ׳</he>, some ed. <he>שכיניכי</he>); a. e.—
<cite ref="Bava Batra 29a:14">B. Bath. 29ᵃ</cite> <he>ש׳ מידע ידעי וכ׳</he> Ms. M. (ed. <he>ידיע</he>, corr. acc.) neighbors surely know (if people use a house) by day and by night.
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 96b:10">Snh. 96ᵇ</cite> <he>עמון ומואב ש׳ בישי וכ׳</he> Ammon and Moab were bad neighbors of Jerusalem.

Sabb. 109ᵇ ולישלקיה … בי ש׳ let him boil it in beer at the house of one of the neighbors; Ms. M. בשיכרא דש׳ in beer belonging to neighbors; [oth. opin. in Rashi: בי ש׳ at the gleam of sunset, v. שְׁבִיבָא; Var. in Ar. בי שכיבי in the cemetery].—Fem. שֵׁיבַבְתָּא, שְׁבַ׳.
<cite ref="Onkelos Exodus 3:22">Targ. Ex. III, 22</cite> (ed. Berl. <he>שִׁיבָבְ׳</he>; Ms. <he>שַׁבִּיבְ׳</he>, corr. acc.).—
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 97a:7">Snh. 97ᵃ</cite> <he>אתאי שֵׁיבַבְתָּהּ וכ׳</he> a neighbor of hers came and knocked at the door.—Pl. <cite ref="U00785"><he>שֵׁיבְבָתָא</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Ruth 4:17">Targ. Ruth IV, 17</cite> <he>שיבבתאן</he> ed. Lag. (ed. Vien. <he>שֵׁיבַבְתָּן</he>!).
